## funnels

Step-by-step counts for each defined GA4 funnel (currently `sign_in` and
`sign_up`), for a given reporting window.

Each row represents one step of one funnel run, for one relying party (or the
funnel's total across all relying parties).

`Keywords`: Google Analytics, GA4, funnel, funnel step, task success, drop-off,
abandonment, relying party

### Provenance

A funnel is defined as YAML, not SQL: one file per funnel in
[`funnel_src/funnels/`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/tree/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels)
in the `canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline` repo. A dedicated Lambda turns
each funnel's YAML into a GA4 Data API `runFunnelReport` request (via
Workload Identity Federation, same auth pattern as
[`property_traffic`](google_analytics.qmd#property_traffic)) and writes the
result as JSONL. **The YAML on GitHub is the canonical definition of what each
funnel measures** - which pages or events count as which step, in what order,
and over what population. This page describes the table shape; it does not
enumerate step names, because they are versioned in that YAML and can change
between funnel versions.

* **Updated**: Daily, at 06:30 ET (a nightly sweep; see Notes)
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Colin Douglas](mailto:colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://<transformed-bucket>/google_analytics/funnels/`

### Fields

One row per `funnel_id` per `funnel_version` per `window_days` per
`window_end` per `funnelstepname` per `breakdown_value`.

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| funnel_id | string | Partition key. Which funnel this row belongs to (for example, "sign_in", "sign_up") - matches a filename under `funnel_src/funnels/` on GitHub |
| funnel_version | string | Partition key. The funnel definition's version at the time this row was run. A plain integer, but typed `string` by the crawler - see Notes |
| window_days | string | Partition key. Length of the reporting window this row summarizes: "1" for a nightly monitoring run, "7" for a rolling weekly rate |
| window_end | string | Partition key. Last date (inclusive) of the reporting window, as text (for example, "2026-07-23") |
| funnelstepnumber | bigint | The step's 1-indexed position in the funnel |
| funnelstepname | string | The step's name, as declared in the funnel's YAML on GitHub. Not a closed set - see Provenance |
| breakdown_dimension | string | The bare GA4 dimension a funnel's `breakdown:` block splits by (currently always "rp_name", the relying party) |
| breakdown_value | string | The relying party this row covers, or the sentinel `RESERVED_TOTAL` for the funnel's grand total across all relying parties (including any past GA4's 15-value breakdown cap) - see Notes |
| activeusers | bigint | Distinct active users who reached this step, for this relying party, within the window |
| funnelstepcompletionrate | double | GA4's own step-over-step completion rate (this step's users over the previous step's) |
| funnelstepabandonments | bigint | Users who reached this step but did not reach the next one |
| funnelstepabandonmentrate | double | `funnelstepabandonments` as a proportion of this step's `activeusers` |
| window_start | string | First date (inclusive) of the reporting window, as text. Derivable from `window_end` and `window_days`, but stored for convenience |
| window_incomplete | boolean | `true` if this window was trimmed to the funnel's `valid_from`/`valid_to` bounds (see Notes) - **exclude these rows from any trend read as a full window** |

### Notes

**A funnel's step names, order and population can change between versions -
always check GitHub, not a memory of a prior version.** Every CanadaLogin
funnel has already had at least one step renamed or re-scoped since it was
first defined (see the
[task success rate](../cookbook/google_analytics.qmd#task-success-rate)
metric for a worked example). `funnel_version` exists so old and new
definitions coexist rather than silently overwriting each other: **always pin
`funnel_version` in a query**, or use the
[`funnels_current`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels_current) view, which resolves
the newest version per date automatically. Summing or averaging across
versions blends two different definitions of the funnel into one meaningless
number.

**`RESERVED_TOTAL` is a real GA4 sentinel, not a relying party.** A funnel
breakdown caps at 15 distinct values; `RESERVED_TOTAL` is GA4's grand total
across *all* relying parties, including any beyond that cap, and is the
correct number to read as the funnel's overall rate.

**`window_incomplete` rows are written, not dropped, and must be excluded from
a trend.** A window that reaches earlier than a funnel's `valid_from` (or later
than `valid_to`) is trimmed and flagged rather than skipped, so a scheduled job
keeps running as a tagging boundary recedes. A trimmed 7-day row is still
labelled `window_days = "7"` but covers fewer than 7 days - reading it as a
full week understates or overstates the true rate depending on what changed at
the boundary.

**`activeusers` is de-duplicated within its own window and is not additive
across windows.** Summing seven daily (`window_days = "1"`) rows for a week is
not the same query as one `window_days = "7"` row for that week - repeat users
within the week are counted once by the 7-day row and once per day they
appeared by the daily rows. Rates hold close either way; raw counts do not.
Never sum `activeusers` across rows with different `window_end` values.

The nightly 06:30 ET run also self-heals: on a `funnel_version` bump, it
backfills every past window still needed under the new version, so the
"Updated" cadence above describes when new dates land, not necessarily when
every partition was last (re)written.
